newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea sets foreign stock-index futures contracts.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea sets foreign stock-index futures contracts.

text.p: South Korea said on Monday the ceiling for foreign stock-index futures investment would increase to 20,169 contracts in the July 7-31 period.

The Securities Supervisory Board (SSB) earlier said the combined ceiling on foreign investor trading in stock-index futures trade would be raised to 100 percent of the daily average of total open interest during the preceding three months from the current 30 percent.
The ceiling, set at 6,228 contracts in June, would fall to 6,050 contracts on July 1-6 before rising on July 7.
The SSB, however, said the ceiling for individual foreigners would remain at five percent of the daily average number of total open interests.
The individual limit was set at 1,008 contracts for July, compared with 1,038 contracts in June.
The SSB also said the ceiling for foreign stock-index options investment was set at 100,845 contracts for July, while the limit for individual foreigners would be 5,042 contracts.
Options trading is scheduled to begin on July 7.
